To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the D0 values of melanoma cells are the same when assayed by either monolayer or soft agar techniques, but Dq values are different.
the radiation response of melanoma cells was not consistent between assay systems and that Dq values were not similar between cells grown on plastic and cells grown in agar.
The radiation response of human and murine melanoma cells assessed by monolayer and bilayer soft agar is different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new human melanoma cell strain, R83-4, which is a subclone of a human melanoma cell line, R83.
the development of a human melanoma cell strain which will serve as a model for the study of human melanoma in the nude mouse.
the development of an in vitro model system to study the radiosensitivity of melanoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no consistent differences between the radiosensitivity of human and murine melanoma cells asscribed to species differences.
the method of assay does influence the apparent radiation survival of cells and that this influence may be dependent on the cell strain being studied.
the method of assay does influence apparent radiosensitivity and that the D0 values for human melanoma cell lines C8146C and R83-3 are identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the D0 values were similar for human melanomas but different for murine melanomas, and that D0 values were different for cells from all melanomas regardless of species when assayed in monolayer versus agar.
the D0 value is a good index for the radiation response of human melanoma cells, but not for murine melanoma cells.
the radiation response of melanoma cells was influenced by assay system, and that there is no single method of assay which can be used to predict the radiosensitivity of melanomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method used to measure radiation response is an important factor to consider when comparing results from different studies.
the D0 values were similar within 95% for human cells but not murine cells and that Dq values were not similar for any of the cell strains assayed.
the method of assay should be taken into account when comparing radiation sensitivity data between different laboratories.
